title: while Loops and Repeated Execution
learningObjectives: Explain the key idea in while loops and repeated execution.
Identify the relevant syntax and rules.
Trace each example and predict the result.
Apply the concept in a small program.
Avoid a common mistake related to this topic.

understand.concept: A while loop repeats a block while its condition remains true. The condition is checked before each iteration, so the loop may run zero times. A loop must make progress toward termination.
understand.whyItMatters: Loops automate repeated tasks such as validation, counting, processing and menu interaction.
understand.analogy: Think of this as a control or calculation rule that tells a program how to handle a particular situation consistently.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a starting point; C++ syntax, types and execution rules determine actual behaviour.
understand.explain:
## Condition-controlled repetition
A while loop checks the condition before entering each iteration. If it is false initially, the body is skipped.

## Progress
Update state so the condition eventually becomes false. A missing update can cause an infinite loop.

## Input validation
A loop can repeat a prompt until valid input is received, but robust input handling should also consider stream failure and clearing invalid input.

examples.code: int i{1}, sum{0};\nwhile (i <= 4) { sum += i; ++i; }\nstd::cout << sum;
examples.explanation: The loop accumulates values and finishes with sum 10.

examples.title: Sentinel concept
examples.explanation: A sentinel value can indicate that repetition should end.
